_meta.description: Goa statewide labour-market indicators from the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) Annual Report July 2023 - June 2024, Appendix-A state tables. All rates are in per cent, usual status (ps+ss), age 15 years and above, rural+urban, unless a field name says otherwise.
_meta.source: NSO/MoSPI, Annual Report PLFS 2023-24 (July 2023 - June 2024): Table 16 (LFPR, 15+) PDF p.125; Table 16 (LFPR 15-29) PDF p.123; Table 17 (WPR, 15+) PDF p.130; Table 18 (UR 15-29) PDF p.133; Table 18 (UR 15+) PDF p.135; Table 27 (industry by NIC-2008 section, rural+urban persons) PDF p.237; Table 35 (non-agricultural workers by enterprise type) PDF pp.276, 279, 282; Table 32 (UR, current weekly status) PDF p.260.
_meta.definition: Usual status (principal status + subsidiary status, ps+ss), persons aged 15 years and above. Youth = age 15-29, same definition.
_meta.granularity_note: PLFS publishes no district-level estimates. Goa's sample is small (Table 35 lists 545 sampled non-agricultural workers: 209 rural, 336 urban), so the sub-group rates (female, youth, rural/urban) have wide sampling error. Use the Census 2011 file for district contrasts.
_meta.why_not_newer: PLFS moved to a calendar-year design in 2025, and no July 2024 - June 2025 annual report exists. The Annual Report PLFS 2025 (Jan-Dec 2025, released 2026-03-26/27) is the newest release, but I could not retrieve its full state tables; the MoSPI press note (https://www.mospi.gov.in/uploads/latestReleases/latest_release_1774607827733_3e8964a9-268b-4cc9-ad65-cfc8a9e32f08_Press_note_AR_PLFS_2025_23032025_V2.1_26032026_final.pdf) has no state figures. MoSPI says 2025 estimates are not strictly comparable with the earlier annual reports. See latest_headline_2025.
_meta.cross_check: The press-reported Goa figure of 8.7% for 2023-24 (Herald Goa) is the current weekly status (CWS) rate for age 15+ (Table 32: 8.7). The usual-status rate is 8.5.

sector_employment._note: % of usually working persons (ps+ss), all ages, rural+urban (Table 27). agriculture = NIC section A; manufacturing_and_industry = B mining 1.18 + C manufacturing 17.80 + D electricity 0.92 + E water/waste 0.61; construction = F; services = sections G-T summed (17.05 trade + 7.11 transport + 11.00 accommodation & food + 0.67 + 1.24 + 2.26 + 1.64 + 1.13 + 3.94 public admin + 6.14 education + 2.50 health + 0.27 + 0.73 + 3.46 households). The published sections add to 100.02 because of rounding.

statewide._informal_note: Share of non-agricultural workers (NIC divisions 05-99, ps+ss) in proprietary and partnership enterprises (Table 35). If employer's households are also counted as informal, rural stays 50.6 and urban becomes 56.9. This measures the informal SECTOR, not informal employment.

youth_15_29._note: Table 18, Table 16 and Table 17 (age 15-29, ps+ss). All-India youth UR for comparison: 10.2.

latest_headline_2025.note: The Goa figure of 8.3% (age 15+, usual status, reported as the highest among states) comes from press coverage (Goemkarponn, 6 Apr 2026: https://goemkarponn.com/goa-tops-india-in-unemployment-rate-at-8-3-plfs-report-reveals/). I did not check it against the report's state table. The all-India 3.1% and 9.9% come from the MoSPI press note. Goa's 2025 youth rate was not found, so it is null. The rural/urban split in that article looked inconsistent and was not used.
